Data Science eventually leaves the notebook.

Models run on servers. Jobs write logs. Environments break. Files become too large to open manually.

That is where CLI fluency pays off.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key ideas
`grep` `find` `sort` `uniq` `wc` `cut` `awk` `sed`
`ssh` `scp` `curl` `tar` `ps` `top` `kill` `PATH` `venv`
:::

## Inspect data without opening it

```bash
head -5 data.csv
wc -l data.csv
du -h data.csv
grep "missing" pipeline.log
```

Find files:

```bash
find . -name "*.parquet"
```

Watch a running job:

```bash
tail -f training.log
```

## Understand redirection

```bash
python train.py > train.log 2>&1
```

means:

```text
stdout ─┐
        ├──▶ train.log
stderr ─┘
```

This tiny idea is enormously useful for long-running jobs.

## Environments

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Know which Python is executing:

```bash
which python
python --version
python -m pip --version
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Professional checkpoint
You do not need to become a Linux administrator. For DS/ML, aim to navigate confidently, inspect files/logs, manage environments, understand processes, use SSH, and compose small shell pipelines.
:::
